rejection_findings.finding: The block assigns Cratylus's substantive handoff to 428a, although Hermogenes speaks there and Cratylus begins at 428b-c.

revisions.title: Cratylus answers the summons — and the thesis meets an image test
revisions.body: At 428a, Hermogenes—not Cratylus—answers the summons, quoting Hesiod to urge Socrates to keep contributing. Socrates then opens the floor at 428b, inviting Cratylus to supply a better account and even offering to become his pupil. Cratylus's substantive reply arrives in 428b-c: he accepts the invitation while casting Socrates' speech as inspired. The thesis soon becomes testable: Cratylus makes false speech impossible, and Socrates sets names beside portraits and other images, making the question of correct likeness concrete. The exchange turns apparent deference into argumentative pressure.
